newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lamfalussy repeats support for euro-zone council.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy repeats support for euro-zone council.

text.p: The future European Central Bank and governments in European monetary union must have a means of talking to each other, European Monetary Institute head Alexandre Lamfalussy said in an interview with daily Liberation published on Monday.
While the Maastricht treaty prevented governments from influencing the policies of the independent central bank, "there will be practical problems in some areas", he said.
"To resolve these, a dialogue must be set up between the ECB and the council of ministers which exercises power in other areas of economic policy," he added.

"Shouldn't we think about a kind of council of economy and finance ministers where only the ministers of the euro zone are present. Suppose that monetary union starts with nine countries, they will have one single monetary policy, but for other policies a decision will have to be taken by 15 (countries).

"It is not realistic, since, in some situations the interests of the nine countries in the euro zone will not necessarily be the same as those of the 15. Therefore the ECB and the governments in the euro zone must be able to talk to each other," he said.

France's proposal for a stability council to co-ordinate policies among countries in the euro zone has come under fire from the Bundesbank which fears it might be used to undermine the independence of the ECB.
